pthm-cm13-flow-preservation.title: "The Hamiltonian evolution of a potential presentation preserves the two-form, the bracket and the determinant on its actual time-slice domains, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time"
pthm-cm13-flow-preservation.physical_scope: "Preservation of the symplectic structure by the model's Hamiltonian evolution: on the actual time-slice domains of a $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian, also for a time-dependent Hamiltonian, the solution map is a canonical map of the presentation, preserves the bracket of $C^{2}$ phase functions and has unit determinant; hence the model's potential-branch flow preserves the presentation's two-form locally in time. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; no completeness of the flow, no all-time assertion and no measured value is claimed."

pthm-cm13-generating-functions.title: "Generating functions for a potential presentation: first- and second-kind data generate canonical maps locally, the local converse under an invertible projection, and the time-dependent Hamiltonian $K=H+S_t$"
pthm-cm13-generating-functions.physical_scope: "Generating-function theory for the declared potential presentation: first- and second-kind generating functions of the model's canonical charts generate canonical local diffeomorphisms of the presentation with the recorded one-form identities and unit determinant; a canonical diffeomorphism with invertible $(q,Q)$-projection is locally generated in the first kind; and for a time-dependent generating function the transformed Hamiltonian is $K=H+S_t$, with the Hamilton systems of $H$ and $K$ carried into one another by the generated time-dependent map. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global generating function and no empirical content."

pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-t.title: "Integral curves of the presentation's Hamiltonian field are exactly the momentum-phase curves of the model's motions, in every chart; and the forced field is Hamiltonian exactly when the residual force has a velocity-independent potential"
pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-t.physical_scope: "The identification of the model's Hamiltonian evolution with the integral curves of the presentation's Hamiltonian field: on the potential branch the model's motions, the solutions of Hamilton's equations for the branch Hamiltonian and the integral curves of $X_H$ coincide, and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart the declared Lagrange equations coincide with the corresponding Hamilton system; with residual forces the momentum equation carries the force as a source, and the forced field is Hamiltonian exactly when that source derives from a velocity-independent potential. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it makes no existence, uniqueness, completeness or empirical claim."

pthm-cm13-liouville.title: "Liouville's theorem for a potential presentation: the phase-volume form $\\omega^{3N}/(3N)!$ and the Lebesgue measure in each canonical chart are preserved by the Hamiltonian evolution on its actual domains"
pthm-cm13-liouville.physical_scope: "Phase-volume conservation for the declared potential presentation: the top form $\\omega^{3N}/(3N)!$ is nowhere zero and is preserved by every time slice of the $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian evolution, and the Lebesgue measure of every canonical chart is preserved on bounded Borel sets of the actual flow domain, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics, and in its measure-theoretic part it uses the Axiom of Countable Choice exactly where the cited change-of-variables theorem requires it; no empirical content is asserted."

pthm-cm13-observable-evolution.title: "Evolution of phase functions along the model's Hamiltonian solutions: $df/dt=\\partial_t f+\\{f,H\\}$, the first-integral criterion, and the closed bracket algebra of autonomous first integrals"
pthm-cm13-observable-evolution.physical_scope: "The evolution identity of the declared potential presentation: along the model's Hamiltonian solutions the total time derivative of a phase function is its explicit time derivative plus the bracket with the branch Hamiltonian; autonomous functions with vanishing bracket are constant on trajectories, and, for an autonomous Hamiltonian, the bracket of two autonomous $C^{3}$ first integrals is again a first integral and the Hamiltonian itself is a first integral. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content."

pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic.title: "The two-form of a potential presentation is closed and nondegenerate, and each generalized-coordinate momentum chart carries the same symplectic structure: $\\Phi_X^*\\lambda=\\sum P_a\\,dq^a$ and $\\Phi_X^*\\omega=\\sum dq^a\\wedge dP_a$"
pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic.physical_scope: "The symplectic structure of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: on the Cartesian momentum phase chart the two-form $\\omega=\\sum dx^a\\wedge dp_a$ is closed and nondegenerate, and on each declared generalized-coordinate momentum chart the pullback of the presentation's two-form along the presentation's own chart map has the canonical coordinate expression. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no dynamics, no conservation law and no measured value."

pthm-cm14-action-angle.title: "Action-angle coordinates of a completely integrable presentation: period-one angles, action coordinates, $H=h(I)$ and linear motion on the tori"
pthm-cm14-action-angle.physical_scope: "Action-angle coordinates for a completely integrable datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: near a compact connected regular fibre and over a ball of regular values on which the integral map is a proper submersion with connected fibres, there are period-one angle and action coordinates of the presentation's two-form with $\\omega=\\sum_i d\\theta_i\\wedge dI_i$; fibrewise-constant functions, in particular the datum and the branch Hamiltonian, depend on the actions alone; and the model's motions become the constant-action, linear-angle flows. The conclusion is conditional on the Axiom of Countable Choice, on the complete integrability of the datum and on all the fibre hypotheses; it is local over the ball of regular values, asserts no global coordinates on the phase domain, and carries no empirical content. The identification of the coordinates with classical period integrals is a normalization convention, not part of the theorem."

pthm-cm14-adiabatic-invariance.title: "Adiabatic invariance of the action of a slowly varying one-frequency model: an order-$\\varepsilon$ drift bound on the $O(1/\\varepsilon)$ time scale"
pthm-cm14-adiabatic-invariance.physical_scope: "Adiabatic invariance of the action coordinate of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch when the model carries a slow real parameter: if in a period-one action-angle chart the branch Hamiltonian is $h(I,s)+\\varepsilon k(I,\\theta,s)$ with nonvanishing frequency $|\\partial_Ih|\\ge\\omega_0$ and the parameter runs as $s(t)=s_0+\\varepsilon t$, then along every model solution that stays in the compact chart region the action changes by at most the displayed order-$\\varepsilon$ bound on $0\\le t\\le A/\\varepsilon$. The statement is conditional on the existence of the uniform parameter-dependent action-angle chart, on the frequency bound and on the trapping of the solution; it asserts no exact invariance, no statement across a separatrix or a chart boundary, and no empirical content."

pthm-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-characteristic.title: "A complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation produces the model's motions, its Jacobi constants and local canonical $(\\beta,\\alpha)$ labels"
pthm-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-characteristic.physical_scope: "The characteristics theorem of the Hamilton-Jacobi method for a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: from a complete integral of the presentation's Hamilton-Jacobi equation in a fixed momentum chart, the characteristic curves of the equation solve the chart's Hamilton equations; on the potential branch they are motions of the model; the derivatives of the complete integral in the parameters are constant along them; a local converse solves the constants equation for the configuration; and the Jacobi data are local canonical coordinates of the presentation's two-form. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it is local in the time, configuration and parameter variables, assumes the nondegeneracy of the mixed derivative at the base point only, and asserts no global solution, no completeness and no empirical content."

pthm-cm14-regular-tori.title: "Compact connected regular fibres of a completely integrable datum of the presentation are Lagrangian tori with a full period lattice"
pthm-cm14-regular-tori.physical_scope: "The fibre structure of a completely integrable datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: a compact connected regular common fibre of the integral map is an embedded Lagrangian submanifold generically spanned by the datum's Hamiltonian fields, carries the commuting-field local action of the cited mathematics as a transitive complete action with a full stabilizer lattice, and is diffeomorphic to a torus. The conclusion is conditional on the datum's smoothness, involution, independence on the regular locus, the compactness, connectedness and regularity of the fibre, and on the Axiom of Countable Choice through the cited lattice lemma; it asserts no global fibration, no action-angle coordinates, no completeness of flows off the compact fibre and no empirical content."

pthm-cm15-central-scattering.title: "Finite-range central scattering in the model class: the scattering motion on all of time, the asymptotic velocities and impact parameter $b=J/\\sqrt{2\\mu E}$, the advance $\\Delta$ with deflection $\\pi-2\\Delta$, and the cross-section of a deflection branch"
pthm-cm15-central-scattering.physical_scope: "The scattering prediction of the restricted two-label central model class with a finite-range $C^2$ potential and a simple outer turning point: the relative motion lives on all of time with one apsis and two monotone branches; the asymptotic velocities exist with speed $\\sqrt{2E/\\mu}$; beyond the range the branches are exactly free and the incoming and outgoing lines have perpendicular distance $b=J/\\sqrt{2\\mu E}$; the half-angle advance is the stated quadrature and the asymptotic directions satisfy the deflection relation with angle $\\pi-2\\Delta$ when $0<\\Delta<\\pi/2$; and on a smooth deflection branch that records the model's deflections the outgoing angular measure has cross-section density $b|\\mathrm db/\\mathrm d\\theta|/\\sin\\theta$ and the expected uniform-incident rate is the flux times the truncated cross-section. The result is a conditional deduction inside the adopted model class; it uses the model data $E,J,u$ and no measured value, asserts no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, and reports no detection."

pthm-cm15-control-volume-balance.title: "The smooth open-flow model: moving-control-region mass and momentum balances, their material and fixed special cases, and the inlet/outlet decomposition reproducing the open-body and rocket laws"
pthm-cm15-control-volume-balance.physical_scope: "The moving-control-region bookkeeping of the adopted smooth open-flow model: under the adopted material mass and momentum balances for every material subregion, a non-material control region has the stated mass and momentum rates with boundary speed $w$, the material and fixed special cases follow, and under an inlet/outlet split of the boundary the flux terms become the entering and leaving mass rates with flux-averaged inertial velocities, so that the lumped open body obeys the material accounting and rocket law adopted in the impulse postulate. The balances are adopted hypotheses of this item, not derivations from particle mechanics; the result asserts no constitutive law, no boundary condition, no measured value and no observational claim."

pthm-cm15-impact-balance.title: "Consequences of the adopted impact and open-mass models: continuity of total momentum, the smooth-force exclusion, the restitution solution with $\\Delta K=-\\frac{1-e^2}{2}\\mu\\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\\rVert_2^2$, and the open-body and rocket laws"
pthm-cm15-impact-balance.physical_scope: "The conditional consequences of the page's adopted impact and open-mass extensions: total momentum is continuous across an isolated reciprocal impulse with the impulse removed from the second label; a smooth-force motion with continuous force maps cannot carry a nonzero impulse, so the contact model is an extension rather than a smooth-force theorem; a collinear contact with coefficient of restitution $e\\in[0,1]$ has the stated post-impact velocities and kinetic-energy change, is dissipative for $e<1$, and its contact law is an independent assumption not derivable from momentum balance; and the open-body material accounting yields the derived law $mv'=F+r_{\\mathrm{in}}(w_{\\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\\mathrm{out}}(w_{\\mathrm{out}}-v)$ with the rocket thrust as the special case. The result is a conditional deduction from adopted model data; it asserts no measured value of $e$, the impulse or the mass rates, and identifies no observed dissipation mechanism."

pthm-cm15-rutherford-model.title: "Repulsive Coulomb scattering in the model class: global non-colliding motion, the deflection map $\\theta=2\\arctan(\\kappa/(2Eb))$, the Rutherford density $(\\kappa/4E)^2\\csc^4(\\theta/2)$, finite angular cutoffs and the divergent ideal total"
pthm-cm15-rutherford-model.physical_scope: "The Coulomb specialisation of the page's finite-range scattering statement, as a model prediction: the repulsive $\\kappa/r$ potential has a unique simple outer turning point and every relative motion of the stated data extends to all of time without collision, with asymptotic velocities of speed $\\sqrt{2E/\\mu}$ and asymptotic impact distance $b=J/\\sqrt{2\\mu E}$; the deflection map is the $C^1$ decreasing bijection $2\\arctan(\\kappa/(2Eb))$ with a single branch, the differential cross-section is the Rutherford density $(\\kappa/4E)^2\\csc^4(\\theta/2)$, every angular band has the finite truncated cross-section $\\pi(b(\\theta_1)^2-b(\\theta_2)^2)$, and the ideal total cross-section diverges at forward angles. The parameter $\\kappa$ is a model datum of the mechanical model and is not identified with any electromagnetic quantity; the result reports no measurement, no screening law and no capture, radiation, relativistic or quantum modification."

pthm-cm16-energy-stability-and-instabili.title: "Energy stability and instability of the mechanical model at an equilibrium: the strict minimum is Lyapunov stable, a negative Hessian eigenvalue gives linear instability, a strictly concave potential gives nonlinear instability, and exact energy conservation rules out attraction"
pthm-cm16-energy-stability-and-instabili.physical_scope: "The stability consequences of the mechanical chart data at a mechanical equilibrium q0: a strict local minimum of the potential gives a Lyapunov stable equilibrium; a negative Hessian eigenvalue gives an unbounded solution of the linearised variational equation (linear instability, with no nonlinear conclusion); a negative definite Hessian (strict local maximum) makes the equilibrium unstable in the nonlinear sense through the hyperbolic instability theorem; and exact energy conservation along the model's motions prevents asymptotic stability whenever states of different energy accumulate at the equilibrium, so a strict minimum is stable but not attracting. No global stability, no asymptotic stability and no statement about degenerate (zero-eigenvalue) Hessians is claimed."

pthm-cm16-hyperbolic-linearization.title: "Hyperbolic linearisation of an equilibrium of the model: exponential dichotomy of the linearised flow, local exponential asymptotic stability in the stable case, and instability in the saddle case"
pthm-cm16-hyperbolic-linearization.physical_scope: "The consequences of the hyperbolic linearisation of an equilibrium state of an autonomous model whose force map is of class C1 in the state: invariant stable and unstable subspaces of the linearised flow with exponential estimates and exponential separation from the equilibrium; local exponential asymptotic stability of the equilibrium when the whole spectrum lies in the open left half-plane; and instability when no eigenvalue lies on the imaginary axis and one lies in the open right half-plane. The rates and constants belong to the linearised flow in the declared state chart; no centre-case, global, parameter-uniform or empirical statement is made."

pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-m.title: "Poincare recurrence for the model's Hamiltonian flow on a bounded invariant set of finite phase volume: almost every state of any Borel subset returns to it infinitely often"
pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-m.physical_scope: "Poincare recurrence for the Hamiltonian flow of a declared autonomous potential presentation: if a bounded Borel set of phase space with finite Lebesgue measure is invariant under the flow (as happens for the compact energy sublevel sets of a trapped one-dimensional model), then for every Borel subset of it almost every state returns to that subset infinitely often at integer multiples of the time unit. The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice, inherited from the phase-volume preservation theorem, and it asserts nothing about return times, about which states return, about infinite phase volume or incomplete flows, and nothing empirical."

pthm-cm16-separatrix-splitting-and-horse.title: "A smooth periodically forced one-coordinate model with a transverse homoclinic horseshoe: the physical stroboscopic map has a compact invariant set conjugate to the shift, chaotic in the stated sense"
pthm-cm16-separatrix-splitting-and-horse.physical_scope: "The conditional chaos theorem for one declared smooth mechanical model: a single label of fixed positive mass on a line, subject to the harmonic restoring force plus a smooth P-periodic polynomial pulse forcing derived from an explicit bump function. For every pulse width below a threshold depending only on the dimensionless amplitude parameter a>=100 and the bump, the physical stroboscopic map of the model has a compact invariant set on which it is conjugate to the two-sign shift, is topologically mixing, has dense periodic points and sensitive dependence, with two hyperbolic fixed points and transverse homoclinic points, and all coded states satisfy the explicit bounds |Q|<=sqrt(a+3) l0 and |Pi|<=m l0 w0 sqrt(a+3). The model is an adopted mechanical model, not a reported apparatus; no measurement, no empirical chaos claim and no claim about other driven or nearly integrable models is made."

pthm-cm16-variational-equation-and-linea.title: "Linearisation along a motion of the mechanical model: the flow derivative solves the variational equation, with Lipschitz dependence, the constant-metric second-order form, and the conditional finite-time error bound of the linear approximation"
pthm-cm16-variational-equation-and-linea.physical_scope: "The linearisation of the mechanical chart model along a declared motion: the derivative of the model's local flow with respect to the initial state solves the variational equation along the motion; nearby initial states separate at most exponentially with the Lipschitz constant of the field; for a constant kinetic metric the second-order linearisation is M eta'' = -D^2 U(x(t)) eta; and whenever the quantitative quadratic remainder and linear growth bounds are declared on a ball, the finite-time difference between the nonlinear motion and the solution of the linearised equation obeys the supplier's explicit bound. The constants C and L are declared model-data bounds; no measured value, no long-time approximation and no global statement is asserted."

pthm-cm17-elastic-plane-wave-speeds.title: "Plane elastic waves in the adopted model: the dispersion condition and the longitudinal and transverse speeds"
pthm-cm17-elastic-plane-wave-speeds.physical_scope: "Conditional on the small-strain isotropic linear elastic branch: a plane displacement wave a cos(<k,x> - omega t) satisfies the model's displacement equation with zero body force on all of space-time if and only if the dispersion relation rho_0 omega^2 a = mu_s |k|^2 a + (lambda + mu_s) <k,a> k holds; parallel amplitudes give the longitudinal speed root((lambda+2mu_s)/rho_0) and orthogonal amplitudes give the transverse speed root(mu_s/rho_0), both real and positive under the branch's positivity hypotheses. The theorem asserts no completeness of plane waves, no measured modulus and no empirical value."

pthm-cm17-incompressible-periodic-local-.title: "Local existence, uniqueness and pressure reconstruction for the incompressible fluid model on the periodic cell"
pthm-cm17-incompressible-periodic-local-.physical_scope: "Conditional on the adopted incompressible Newtonian (or inviscid Euler) fluid branch and its periodic-cell idealization, and on the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the Fourier machinery: for smooth divergence-free periodic initial velocity data of finite H^s norm (integer s at least 4) there is a local time T depending only on that norm, and a smooth periodic velocity and a unique smooth mean-zero pressure satisfying the model's field equations exactly; the velocity is unique on the interval among smooth divergence-free solutions, depends continuously on initial data in H^{s-1}, and no all-time bound or global regularity conclusion is claimed. The theorem concerns the Eulerian field equations and does not construct the material label map; no measured viscosity or pressure is asserted."

pthm-cm17-linear-elastic-equation-of-mot.title: "The displacement equation of the linear elastic branch: rho_0 partial_t^2 xi = rho_0 b + mu_s Laplacian xi + (lambda + mu_s) grad div xi"
pthm-cm17-linear-elastic-equation-of-mot.physical_scope: "Conditional on the adopted mass and momentum balances and on the adopted small-strain isotropic linear elastic constitutive branch: in the material description of a small displacement field xi, the model's momentum equation is exactly rho_0 partial_t^2 xi = rho_0 b + mu_s Laplacian xi + (lambda + mu_s) grad div xi, with the second spatial derivatives of xi continuous and the material and spatial variables identified to first order as part of the branch's small-displacement idealization. The theorem is a conditional identity of the model; it asserts no solution existence, no error bound for the small-displacement replacement and no measured modulus."

pthm-cm17-momentum-equation.title: "The momentum equation of the continuum model: local form rho D_t u = rho b + div sigma"
pthm-cm17-momentum-equation.physical_scope: "Conditional on the adopted mass-balance and momentum-balance postulates and on the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the transport and divergence machinery: the force-form balance on every admissible region, together with the continuity equation and the transport identity, is equivalent to the local momentum equation rho D_t u = rho b + div sigma on the current regions, where sigma is the stress matrix produced by the balance principles. The result is a conditional model deduction; it asserts no existence of solutions, no constitutive relation and no measured value."

pthm-cm17-stress-matrix-and-symmetry.title: "Existence, uniqueness and symmetry of the stress matrix from the adopted balance principles"
pthm-cm17-stress-matrix-and-symmetry.physical_scope: "Conditional on the adopted force model and balance principles: on every bounded spatial region inside the current configuration the continuous traction field is represented by a unique continuous stress matrix, the reversed-normal identity t(-n) = -t(n) holds, and the couple-free torque balance forces the stress matrix to be symmetric. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted balance principles and the cited mathematical Cauchy-tetrahedron and angular-balance theorems; it asserts no positivity, no constitutive relation and no measured stress."

rem-cm01-model-limit.title: "Status audit and model limits of the framework page: primitive data, adopted assumptions, derived objects and what is not claimed"
rem-cm01-model-limit.physical_scope: "A status audit and scope remark for the framework-and-geometry page: which objects are primitive model data, which statements are adopted postulates, which are constructed or proved, and which physical claims are deliberately not made here. Bookkeeping only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no claim about nature beyond the items it cites."

rem-cm02-open-system-warning.title: "Status audit and model boundaries of the force page: open systems, frame selection, breakdown and empirical scope"
rem-cm02-open-system-warning.physical_scope: "A scope and status audit of the force page: which objects are adopted model data, which statements are conditional deductions, which computations are examples, and which claims are deliberately not made; the boundary between the declared particle labels and their environment in an open-system description; the frame-selection content of external fields and apparatus; the empirical status of force-law parameters, drag regimes and model comparisons. Bookkeeping and scope only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no claim about nature beyond the items it cites."

rem-cm03-conservation-scope.title: "Status audit and scope of the balance page: conditional conservation, open systems, frames, potential normalization and empirical boundaries"
rem-cm03-conservation-scope.physical_scope: "A scope and status audit of the balance page: which objects are defined, which statements are conditional deductions from the force and interaction posts, which hypotheses each conservation statement needs, and which claims are deliberately not made; the frame dependence of the conserved quantities, the open-system boundary, the normalization of a potential, the local-versus-global potential distinction and the empirical status of model parameters. Bookkeeping and scope only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no conservation beyond the items it cites."

rem-cm04-linear-model-scope.title: "Scope and limits of the one-dimensional conservative and dissipative models: declared class, approximation status, empirical parameters and open extensions"
rem-cm04-linear-model-scope.physical_scope: "An audit of the page's conditional content: which statements are declared model assumptions, which are exact conditional deductions of the model, and which are approximation or empirical interfaces; the status of the linear models as idealizations, the finite-time character of the small-angle bound, the phenomenological character of the drag with its neglected fluctuations, the prescribed-drive idealization, and the handling of measured parameters as empirical premises. The remark asserts no new mathematical or physical claim and no measured value."

rem-cm05-collision-scope.title: "Scope of the two-body and central-force page: collision and radial exclusions, point-particle and finite-size limits, the empirical parameters and their uncertainty, and the conditional status of the orbit statements"
rem-cm05-collision-scope.physical_scope: "A scope and status audit of the two-body, central-force and gravitation page: which items are adopted assumptions, which are conditional deductions, which exclusions (collision, radial motion, finite size, external bodies, relativistic regime) the statements carry, how the empirical parameters $G_{\\mathrm N}$ and the mass identification qualify numerical conclusions, and which claims are deliberately not made. Bookkeeping and scope only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no conclusion beyond the items it cites."

rem-cm06-dalembert-vakonomic-distinction.title: "The d'Alembert and vakonomic prescriptions are different models: what is proved, what is adopted, and which questions are open"
rem-cm06-dalembert-vakonomic-distinction.physical_scope: "Scope remark distinguishing the two prescriptions for a velocity-constrained model: the d'Alembert (Chetaev, frozen-kernel) law adopted by this framework's nonholonomic models and the vakonomic (stationary augmented action) prescription, with the proved discrepancy for the model z'=xy', the exclusion of silent constraint substitution, and the open questions of rank and contact changes, rolling models and empirical adequacy. The remark asserts no measured value and no experimental comparison."

rem-cm07-scope-and-singular-warnings.title: "Scope of the stationary-action formulation: no minimisation, regular mechanical Lagrangians, nonholonomic exclusions and empirical status"
rem-cm07-scope-and-singular-warnings.physical_scope: "Scope audit of the stationary-action formulation of the force model: stationarity is not minimisation; the mechanical Lagrangians of this framework are regular and the chart Legendre map is hyperregular, so the second-order equations determine accelerations, while degenerate Lagrangians are excluded; the unrestricted action principle is not available for velocity constraints and is refuted by the cited counterexample; and the stationary-action equivalence is a conditional theorem of the model, not empirical evidence. The remark asserts no new physical claim."

rem-cm08-external-symmetry-breaking.title: "Scope of the symmetry-conservation statements: force laws that break kinematic symmetries, residual forces, moving coordinates and the empirical boundary"
rem-cm08-external-symmetry-breaking.physical_scope: "Scope audit of the symmetry and conservation statements of the pair: the symmetry criteria are conditions on the model's declared Lagrangian and potential, not on the kinematic framework; force laws with external or confining potentials break the corresponding charges, with the failure rates computed by the sharpness clauses; residual forces destroy conservation of a symmetry charge unless they pair to zero with the generator along the motion; in a moving coordinate description the conserved chart energy function need not be the inertial mechanical energy; time-dependent potentials break energy conservation; and no converse from an observed conservation to a symmetry of a model, and no empirical claim, is asserted. The remark adds no new physical claim."

rem-cm09-zero-modes-degeneracy-and-scope.title: "Scope of the coupled quadratic model: zero modes, degenerate eigenspaces, unstable quadratic directions and the limits of the approximation statements"
rem-cm09-zero-modes-degeneracy-and-scope.physical_scope: "Scope and cautionary reading of the coupled quadratic model of this page: the meaning of a zero modal stiffness (an affine, non-oscillatory free direction, with quadratic-in-time growth under a constant force component), the intrinsic status of degenerate eigenspaces and the non-intrinsic status of individual mode vectors, the exponential directions of an indefinite stiffness and the conditional nonlinear instability of a hyperbolic equilibrium, and the limits of the page's approximation statements (the quadratic model is exact only for quadratic data, the linearization error bound is finite-time and small-data, and the averaging estimate holds on the O(1/epsilon) time scale under explicit smallness and trapping hypotheses). The item records no measurement, asserts no empirical applicability of any model, and makes no stability claim beyond the explicitly cited conditional conclusions."

rem-cm12-singular-models.title: "Scope of the Legendre transformation: singular velocity Hessians, regular versus hyperregular presentations, and the excluded constraint theory"
rem-cm12-singular-models.physical_scope: "A scope audit of the Legendre and Hamiltonian constructions of this page for a declared potential presentation of the force branch: which presentations are excluded by a singular velocity Hessian, why the mechanical branch of the framework is never singular, the separation between regular and hyperregular presentations, the fact that only eliminated holonomic constraints are covered, and the empirical status of the vocabulary. The remark asserts no new physical claim and reports no measurement."

rem-cm13-locality-topology.title: "Scope of the symplectic and canonical methods for a potential presentation: locality of generating functions, projections and determinant tests, absent global claims, and empirical status"
rem-cm13-locality-topology.physical_scope: "Scope of the symplectic and canonical machinery for the declared potential presentation: the local character of generating functions and their projection hypotheses, the determinant tests and the failure of canonicity for volume-preserving maps in dimension at least four, the absence of global generating functions in general, the local-in-time character of flow preservation, the choice assumption in the measure-theoretic volume statement, and the purely conditional empirical status of the whole page. The remark asserts no mathematical claim beyond the items it cites."

rem-cm14-scope-of-hamilton-jacobi-and-in.title: "Scope of the Hamilton-Jacobi and integrability statements: locality, the fibre hypotheses, global obstructions and the frequency conventions"
rem-cm14-scope-of-hamilton-jacobi-and-in.physical_scope: "The recorded scope of the Hamilton-Jacobi and integrability items of this page: the local character of the Hamilton-Jacobi construction and of its no-caustic hypothesis; the separate requirements of involution and independence in complete integrability; the compactness, connectedness, regularity and proper-submersion hypotheses of the torus and action-angle conclusions together with their Countable-Choice assumption; the published monodromy obstruction to global action-angle coordinates; and the period-one versus radian frequency convention. The remark asserts no new mathematical claim and no empirical content; it is a scope record for the conditional deductions of this page."

rem-cm15-model-boundaries.title: "Scope of the scattering and impulse items: model boundaries, branch and cutoff qualifications, and the claims deliberately not made"
rem-cm15-model-boundaries.physical_scope: "A scope remark recording which claims the page's scattering, impact and open-flow items make, which model assumptions they adopt, and which claims they deliberately do not make: no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, no counting or probability interpretation of the cross-section, no contact scattering as a smooth-potential theorem, no measured values or electromagnetic identification of the Coulomb parameter, no laboratory-frame statement without the boost, no attractive capture, screening, radiation, inelastic, relativistic or quantum modifications, and no constitutive or boundary law for the open flow. The remark adds no claim of its own beyond the qualifications it records."

rem-cm16-scope-of-stability-and-chaos.title: "Scope of the stability, perturbation and chaos statements: conditional model deductions, the limits of finite-time and numerical evidence, and the empirical qualifications"
rem-cm16-scope-of-stability-and-chaos.physical_scope: "The scope of the page's conditional model deductions: what each stability, linearisation, hyperbolicity, KAM, horseshoe and recurrence statement assumes, what it concludes, which chart and choice conventions it uses, and why numerical trajectories, plotted sections and finite-time growth rates are neither proofs of chaos nor experimental evidence. The remark makes no new mathematical or empirical claim."

rem-cm17-boundary-regularity-and-scope.title: "Boundary data, regularity limits and open scopes of the continuum page, and the model-versus-nature reading"
rem-cm17-boundary-regularity-and-scope.physical_scope: "Scope audit of the continuum page: the ideal boundary data used by its theorems (periodic cell, fixed ends, whole line, and the no-slip condition of the channel example), the smoothness and positive-Jacobian hypotheses that exclude shocks, interfaces and corners, the validity regimes of the three constitutive branches, the open specialist scopes deliberately not claimed (general compressible entropy systems, rough walls and boundary layers, nonlinear constitutive PDEs, turbulence closure, all-time three-dimensional regularity), and the model-versus-nature status of every result on the page. The remark asserts no new physical claim, no measurement and no theorem."

rem-cm18-em-bridge.title: "The electromagnetic bridge: what a charged-particle coupling must add to the framework, what the force branch then yields, and what is not imported"
rem-cm18-em-bridge.physical_scope: "A scope remark on the interface between the particle framework and a separately developed electromagnetic model: the additional data a coupling requires (charge attributes with declared dimensions, field maps with domains and regularity, and an added coupling force law), the conditional reuse of the force-branch existence and balance results once such an added force map satisfies the standing hypotheses, and the explicit non-import of field equations, field energy-momentum theorems and coupling-constant values. The item derives no electromagnetic law, predicts no electromagnetic phenomenon and asserts no measured value."

rem-cm18-galilean-regime.title: "The Galilean regime of the framework: frame-relative protocols, the absence of an intrinsic slow-motion parameter, and the empirical status of a validity claim"
rem-cm18-galilean-regime.physical_scope: "A scope remark on the kinematic regime of the framework and its consequences for observable models: the adopted absolute time and Euclidean slices, the Galilean frame changes, the frame-relativity of protocols and prediction maps, and the absence of any intrinsic speed scale or numerical validity cutoff inside the framework. The item asserts no measured speed, no numerical regime boundary and no limit theorem relating the framework to any other model."

rem-cm18-model-test.title: "Model testing for the force branch: what a test specifies, what rejection and retention establish, and what is not claimed"
rem-cm18-model-test.physical_scope: "A scope remark on the logic of testing a force model against data: the ingredients a test must specify, the meaning of a rejection or a retention under a specified model family and sampling model, the distinction between evidence and proof, and the reasons a discrepancy does not by itself identify a failing ingredient. The item reports no measurement, asserts no p-value, no effect size and no empirical conclusion, and makes no claim that any model or law has been tested or confirmed."

rem-cm18-numerical-error.title: "Numerical error in a prediction pipeline: certified velocity-Verlet bounds, additive per-step error, the analytic long-time branch, and the separation from model error"
rem-cm18-numerical-error.physical_scope: "A scope remark on the numerical phase of a prediction pipeline for an operational observable model of the force branch: the certified finite-time discretization and additive per-step error bounds for the velocity-Verlet method, the analytic long-time energy estimates under their holomorphy, step-size and compact-retention hypotheses, and the strict separation of these numerical bounds from the model-versus-nature error and the observation and sampling errors. The item asserts no numerical result for a physical system and no all-time accuracy of any method."

rem-cm18-primary-report-contract.title: "Contract for a future reported experiment of the framework: source, setup, calibration, procedure, sampling, observations, uncertainty and interpretation"
rem-cm18-primary-report-contract.physical_scope: "A scope remark fixing the inventory a future reported experiment of this framework must provide: an actually retrieved primary source, the preparation and apparatus with its calibration data, the measurement protocol in a declared frame, the sampling and selection model, the reported observations with units, the statistical and systematic uncertainty treatment, and a specified comparison model. The item reports no experiment, no observation, no uncertainty and no empirical conclusion; it is a contract for later items, not an experiment."

rem-cm18-qm-bridge.title: "The quantum bridge: a distinct framework, the shape of a quantization or correspondence result, and the absence of any such theorem in this framework"
rem-cm18-qm-bridge.physical_scope: "A scope remark on the relation between this particle framework and a non-relativistic quantum framework: the point-particle idealization that the framework adopts, the ingredients a quantization or correspondence result would need (a reconstruction construction plus limit theorems with explicit domains and hypotheses), and the explicit absence of any such result from this framework. The item derives no quantum statement, predicts no quantum phenomenon, and attaches no quantum interpretation to the probability space of its observable models."
